entries.body:
# Spirit Animal

## Overview
Every Druid walks the wilds in search of harmony, but none walk alone forever. Through ancient rituals and quiet meditation, a Druid eventually encounters a Spirit Animal—a mystical guardian that embodies a single aspect of the natural world. This companion is neither a summoned beast nor a permanent pet, but a spiritual manifestation that willingly answers the Druid's call.

At this rank, your Spirit Animal cannot directly fight alongside you. Instead, it acts as a guide, scout, and conduit between you and the wilderness. It instinctively understands your intentions and communicates through emotions, instincts, and brief spiritual impressions rather than spoken words.

The form of your Spirit Animal is chosen with your Game Master and should reflect your character's personality, beliefs, or connection to nature. A wolf may represent loyalty, an owl wisdom, a fox cunning, or a stag guardianship. Regardless of its form, your companion remains a trusted ally throughout your journey.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

Every Druid walks the wilds in search of harmony, but none walk alone forever. Through ancient rituals and quiet meditation, a Druid eventually encounters a Spirit Animal—a mystical guardian that embodies a single aspect of the natural world. This companion is neither a summoned beast nor a permanent pet, but a spiritual manifestation that willingly answers the Druid's call.

At this rank, your Spirit Animal cannot directly fight alongside you. Instead, it acts as a guide, scout, and conduit between you and the wilderness. It instinctively understands your intentions and communicates through emotions, instincts, and brief spiritual impressions rather than spoken words.

The form of your Spirit Animal is chosen with your Game Master and should reflect your character's personality, beliefs, or connection to nature. A wolf may represent loyalty, an owl wisdom, a fox cunning, or a stag guardianship. Regardless of its form, your companion remains a trusted ally throughout your journey.

---

### Effects

- Spend **15 MP** to summon your **Spirit Animal**.
- The Spirit Animal remains manifested for **10 minutes**.
- Your Spirit Animal is **ethereal** and cannot attack, deal damage, manipulate physical objects, or be targeted by attacks.
- The Spirit Animal may move up to **30 metres** away from you while remaining connected through your spiritual bond.
- You may see and hear through your Spirit Animal's senses as an action. While doing so, your own body is considered **Distracted** and you have **Disadvantage** on Perception Checks made using your own senses.
- The Spirit Animal can silently communicate simple emotions, warnings, and observations to you.
- Gain **+2** to **Nature**, **Survival**, and **Tracking** **D20 Skill Checks** while your Spirit Animal is active.
- Your Spirit Animal instinctively alerts you if it notices:
  - Nearby natural hazards.
  - Dangerous terrain.
  - Wild beasts.
  - Signs of recent natural disturbances.
- The Spirit Animal cannot pass through magical barriers designed to block spirits or extraplanar beings.
- The Spirit Animal cannot enter combat or provide combat bonuses at this rank.

---

### Lore

The first meeting between a Druid and their Spirit Animal is one of the most sacred moments in Druidic tradition. Some encounter their companion beneath ancient trees, others beside tranquil rivers or beneath starlit skies, but every meeting is deeply personal and impossible to forget.

The Spirit Animal is believed to be a fragment of the world's living spirit, choosing its Druid as much as the Druid chooses it. Though incapable of physical interaction at first, it offers guidance, companionship, and perspective drawn from the untamed wilderness itself.

Among the oldest circles, it is said that a Druid who truly understands their Spirit Animal will never again feel lost, no matter how dark the forest or uncertain the path ahead.

---

> *"A Spirit Animal is not the path before you—it is the friend who reminds you why you chose to walk it."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, First Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 2
### Description

Your spiritual bond with your Spirit Animal grows stronger, allowing it to venture farther from your side while sharing more of its instincts and awareness. The connection between your souls becomes increasingly natural, requiring little effort to maintain as you begin to perceive the wilderness through two sets of senses.

Your companion has become far more than a guide. It actively scouts ahead, warns of danger, and instinctively searches for safe paths through unfamiliar terrain. Whether soaring above a dense forest canopy, slipping silently through undergrowth, or climbing rugged cliffs, it serves as an extension of your own awareness.

Although it still cannot physically interact with the world, your Spirit Animal has learned to better interpret the intentions of the creatures and environments it observes. This deeper understanding allows it to provide more accurate warnings and valuable insight before danger reveals itself.

---

### Effects

- Spend **20 MP** to summon your **Spirit Animal**.
- Your Spirit Animal remains manifested for **15 minutes**.
- Your Spirit Animal remains **ethereal**, unable to attack, manipulate objects, or be targeted by conventional attacks.
- Your Spirit Animal may travel up to **60 metres** away from you while maintaining your spiritual bond.
- As an action, you may perceive the world through your Spirit Animal's senses.
- While using your Spirit Animal's senses, your physical body is considered **Distracted** and has **Disadvantage** on Perception Checks using its own senses.
- Gain **+4** to **Nature**, **Survival**, and **Tracking** **D20 Skill Checks** while your Spirit Animal is active.
- Your Spirit Animal instinctively detects:
  - Natural hazards.
  - Dangerous terrain.
  - Nearby beasts.
  - Fresh tracks.
  - Signs of recent movement through the wilderness.
- Your Spirit Animal can distinguish whether nearby creatures appear **calm**, **alert**, **frightened**, or **agitated** through their natural behaviour.
- You may dismiss or resummon your Spirit Animal at any time while the duration remains active without paying an additional Mana Cost.
- The Spirit Animal cannot pass through magical barriers designed to block spirits or extraplanar beings.
- The Spirit Animal cannot enter combat or provide combat bonuses at this rank.

---

### Lore

As the bond deepens, the Spirit Animal begins to think less as a companion and more as an extension of its Druid. Thoughts, emotions, and instincts flow effortlessly between them, allowing each to understand the other without spoken language.

Many Druids describe this stage as learning to trust another set of eyes. While the Spirit Animal explores the wilderness, its discoveries become your own, revealing hidden dangers, forgotten trails, and the subtle movements of the natural world.

The elders teach that this growing trust is essential. A Spirit Animal does not serve its Druid out of obligation—it remains because the bond between them has become one of mutual respect, shared purpose, and unwavering companionship.

---

> *"When two spirits walk as one, even the quietest forest cannot keep its secrets."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, First Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 3
### Description

Your Spirit Animal has become an inseparable extension of your soul, capable of travelling great distances while maintaining an unwavering spiritual connection. The bond between you is now so refined that its instincts, senses, and emotions flow naturally into your own awareness, allowing you to perceive the wilderness with remarkable clarity.

As your companion explores, it does more than simply observe. It studies the land, watches the behaviour of wildlife, and recognises subtle changes within the environment that would escape even experienced hunters. Through your shared bond, these discoveries become your own, enabling you to make informed decisions long before danger reveals itself.

Among the Druidic Circles, reaching this stage is considered a milestone of trust. Your Spirit Animal no longer follows your commands out of duty—it acts as a true partner, anticipating your needs and carrying out your intentions with remarkable understanding.

---

### Effects

- Spend **25 MP** to summon your **Spirit Animal**.
- Your Spirit Animal remains manifested for **20 minutes**.
- Your Spirit Animal remains **ethereal**, unable to attack, manipulate physical objects, or be targeted by conventional attacks.
- Your Spirit Animal may travel up to **100 metres** away from you while maintaining your spiritual bond.
- As an action, you may perceive the world through your Spirit Animal's senses.
- While using your Spirit Animal's senses, your physical body is considered **Distracted** and has **Disadvantage** on Perception Checks made using its own senses.
- Gain **+6** to **Nature**, **Survival**, and **Tracking** **D20 Skill Checks** while your Spirit Animal is active.
- Your Spirit Animal instinctively detects:
  - Natural hazards.
  - Dangerous terrain.
  - Fresh tracks.
  - Nearby beasts.
  - Signs of recent travel through the wilderness.
  - Changes to the surrounding ecosystem caused by natural or unnatural events.
- Your Spirit Animal can distinguish the general behaviour of nearby creatures, recognising whether they are:
  - Hunting.
  - Resting.
  - Fleeing.
  - Defending territory.
  - Travelling.
- You may freely switch between your own senses and your Spirit Animal's senses without ending the ability.
- You may dismiss and resummon your Spirit Animal anywhere within **20 metres** of you while the duration remains active without paying an additional Mana Cost.
- The Spirit Animal cannot pass through magical barriers designed to block spirits or extraplanar beings.
- The Spirit Animal cannot enter combat or provide combat bonuses at this rank.

---

### Lore

Experienced Druids often describe this stage as sharing a single soul between two bodies. Distance becomes increasingly irrelevant as thoughts and instincts flow effortlessly across the spiritual bond, allowing both companions to work together without hesitation or spoken direction.

Many great Wardens relied upon their Spirit Animals to explore dangerous ruins, watch over sacred groves, and guide lost travellers through untamed wilderness. While the Spirit Animal cannot alter the physical world, its watchful presence has prevented countless disasters by revealing dangers before they could unfold.

The oldest Druidic teachings remind every practitioner that trust cannot be forced. Only through patience, respect, and shared purpose does a Spirit Animal choose to become more than a guide—it becomes family.

---

> *"A companion who shares your spirit never walks behind you or before you. They walk beside you, no matter how great the distance."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, First Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 4
### Description

Your Spirit Animal has become a true extension of your spirit, capable of exploring vast distances while maintaining an unbroken bond with you. The connection has evolved beyond shared sight and hearing; emotions, instincts, and awareness flow freely between you both, allowing each to react almost as though you were a single being.

As your companion traverses the wilderness, it perceives far more than simple movement. It recognises disturbances in ecosystems, senses changes in weather before they arrive, and notices subtle shifts in the behaviour of wildlife that often foreshadow approaching danger. Through your bond, these discoveries become instinctive knowledge rather than conscious observation.

Among the ancient Druidic Circles, reaching this stage marks the beginning of true spiritual partnership. A Spirit Animal no longer waits for commands—it understands your intentions and acts independently to protect, guide, and inform, always remaining faithful to the balance of nature.

---

### Effects

- Spend **30 MP** to summon your **Spirit Animal**.
- Your Spirit Animal remains manifested for **25 minutes**.
- Your Spirit Animal remains **ethereal**, unable to attack, manipulate physical objects, or be targeted by conventional attacks.
- Your Spirit Animal may travel up to **150 metres** away while maintaining your spiritual bond.
- As an action, you may perceive the world through your Spirit Animal's senses.
- While using your Spirit Animal's senses, your physical body is considered **Distracted** and has **Disadvantage** on Perception Checks made using its own senses.
- Gain **+8** to **Nature**, **Survival**, and **Tracking** **D20 Skill Checks** while your Spirit Animal is active.
- Your Spirit Animal instinctively detects:
  - Natural hazards.
  - Dangerous terrain.
  - Fresh tracks.
  - Nearby beasts.
  - Signs of recent travel.
  - Changes caused by corruption, blight, or powerful natural disasters.
- Your Spirit Animal can determine the general behaviour of nearby creatures, including whether they are:
  - Hunting.
  - Resting.
  - Defending territory.
  - Travelling.
  - Fleeing.
  - Stalking prey.
- You may freely switch between your own senses and your Spirit Animal's senses without using an action.
- You may dismiss and resummon your Spirit Animal anywhere within **50 metres** of you while the duration remains active without paying an additional Mana Cost.
- While your Spirit Animal is within **10 metres** of you, you gain **Advantage on D20 Perception Checks** relying on sight, hearing, or smell.
- The Spirit Animal cannot pass through magical barriers specifically designed to block spirits or extraplanar beings.
- The Spirit Animal cannot enter combat or provide offensive or defensive combat abilities at this rank.

---

### Lore

To the greatest Druids, the bond between guardian and Spirit Animal becomes impossible to separate. Each instinctively understands the other's purpose, allowing them to explore, observe, and protect the wilderness with extraordinary efficiency.

Many Wardens entrusted with safeguarding sacred groves rely upon their Spirit Animals to patrol vast forests without ever disturbing the delicate balance of nature. The creatures of the wild rarely fear these spiritual companions, often treating them as though they were simply another part of the forest itself.

The oldest teachings claim that when a Druid reaches this stage, the Spirit Animal no longer follows because it was summoned. It remains because the two spirits have chosen to walk the same path for the rest of their lives.

---

> *"When trust is complete, distance loses all meaning. Two spirits become one purpose."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, First Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 5
### Description

Your bond with your Spirit Animal has reached its ultimate expression, transcending that of summoner and companion. You are now two souls united by a single purpose, capable of sharing thoughts, instincts, and senses with effortless clarity. Distance is little more than an inconvenience, and your companion acts with the same wisdom and intent as if it were your own body.

Your Spirit Animal has become the perfect scout and guide, navigating even the most dangerous wilderness without disturbing the balance of nature. It understands your intentions before they are spoken, adapting to changing circumstances and uncovering paths, dangers, and opportunities that would remain invisible to others.

Among the oldest Druidic Circles, those who achieve this mastery are known as **Wildbound Guardians**. Their Spirit Animals are regarded as sacred partners, entrusted with watching over ancient groves, sacred beasts, and places where the natural world remains untouched. Though incapable of direct combat, their presence has saved countless lives through foresight, wisdom, and unwavering vigilance.

---

### Effects

- Spend **35 MP** to summon your **Spirit Animal**.
- Your Spirit Animal remains manifested for **30 minutes**.
- Your Spirit Animal remains **ethereal**, unable to attack, manipulate physical objects, or be targeted by conventional attacks.
- Your Spirit Animal may travel up to **250 metres** away while maintaining your spiritual bond.
- You may freely switch between your own senses and your Spirit Animal's senses without using an action.
- While perceiving through your Spirit Animal, your body remains aware enough to defend itself, removing the **Distracted** condition from previous ranks.
- Gain **+10** to **Nature**, **Survival**, and **Tracking** **D20 Skill Checks** while your Spirit Animal is active.
- Your Spirit Animal instinctively detects:
  - Natural hazards.
  - Dangerous terrain.
  - Fresh tracks.
  - Hidden paths.
  - Nearby beasts.
  - Environmental corruption or blight.
  - Powerful magical disturbances affecting the natural world.
- Your Spirit Animal can determine the general behaviour of nearby creatures, including whether they are:
  - Hunting.
  - Resting.
  - Travelling.
  - Defending territory.
  - Fleeing.
  - Stalking prey.
  - Injured or distressed.
- You may dismiss and resummon your Spirit Animal anywhere within **100 metres** of you while the duration remains active without paying an additional Mana Cost.
- While your Spirit Animal is within **20 metres** of you, you gain **Advantage on D20 Perception, Survival, and Tracking Skill Checks**.
- Your Spirit Animal may communicate complex emotions, instincts, mental images, and simple concepts through your spiritual bond.
- The Spirit Animal cannot pass through magical barriers specifically designed to block spirits or extraplanar beings.
- The Spirit Animal cannot attack, cast spells, manipulate physical objects, or provide direct offensive or defensive combat abilities.

---

### Lore

Few Druids ever reach this level of spiritual harmony. The ancient circles believe that, at this stage, the Spirit Animal is no longer merely a guide gifted by nature, but a reflection of the Druid's own soul. Together they embody the balance between civilisation and wilderness, instinct and wisdom, mortal and spirit.

Throughout Asteria's history, Wildbound Guardians have served as protectors of sacred forests, watchers of ancient world trees, and keepers of forgotten pathways known only to the natural world. Their Spirit Animals have guided refugees through impassable forests, warned entire villages of approaching disasters, and uncovered corruption long before it could take root.

Despite this extraordinary bond, every Druid is reminded that a Spirit Animal is never a servant. It remains a willing companion, choosing each day to walk beside its guardian. That trust, earned through years of respect and shared purpose, is the true source of the talent's power.

---

> *"Strength may win a battle, but trust is what carries two souls across a lifetime. Walk beside your spirit, and neither of you will ever walk alone."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, First Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Prerequisites
None

## Scaling
See individual rank details.

## Synergy
Information coming soon.

## GM Notes
GM-only information coming soon.

entries.body:
# Wild Shape

## Overview
Wild Shape is one of the oldest and most sacred abilities practiced by the Druids of Asteria. Rather than disguising themselves as animals through illusion, Druids temporarily reshape their bodies, minds, and instincts to become one with the creatures they have come to understand.

Learning a new form requires patience, observation, and respect. Before a Druid may transform into a creature, they must first study it in its natural habitat and successfully understand its behaviour, movement, and place within the ecosystem. Only then can its spirit be welcomed into their own.

At this rank, your understanding is limited to simple creatures. Your transformations are best suited for exploration, travel, survival, and escaping danger rather than direct combat. Every new form learned expands your connection with the natural world and lays the foundation for mastering stronger beasts in the future.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

Wild Shape is one of the oldest and most sacred abilities practiced by the Druids of Asteria. Rather than disguising themselves as animals through illusion, Druids temporarily reshape their bodies, minds, and instincts to become one with the creatures they have come to understand.

Learning a new form requires patience, observation, and respect. Before a Druid may transform into a creature, they must first study it in its natural habitat and successfully understand its behaviour, movement, and place within the ecosystem. Only then can its spirit be welcomed into their own.

At this rank, your understanding is limited to simple creatures. Your transformations are best suited for exploration, travel, survival, and escaping danger rather than direct combat. Every new form learned expands your connection with the natural world and lays the foundation for mastering stronger beasts in the future.

---

### Effects

- Spend **25 MP** to transform into a learned Beast Form.
- Wild Shape lasts for **10 minutes** or until dismissed.
- You may only transform into **Small or Medium Beasts** that you have successfully learned.
- To learn a Beast Form, you must:
  - Observe the creature in its natural environment.
  - Study its behaviour and anatomy.
  - Succeed on an appropriate **D20 Nature Check** determined by the Game Master.
- Common beasts require a lower DC than rare or elusive creatures.
- Once a Beast Form has been learned, it is permanently added to your Wild Shape forms.
- While transformed:
  - You gain the beast's natural movement types (such as climbing or swimming).
  - You retain your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma.
  - You cannot cast spells.
  - You cannot speak languages unless your Game Master determines the form is capable of doing so.
  - Your equipment merges into your new form and provides no benefits unless specifically stated otherwise.
- If your transformed form is reduced to **0 HP**, Wild Shape immediately ends and you return to your normal form. Any remaining damage carries over to your normal Hit Points.
- You may voluntarily end Wild Shape at any time without using an action.

---

### Lore

The first successful Wild Shape is celebrated within every Druidic Circle as a rite of passage. It marks the moment a Druid ceases to merely observe nature and instead experiences life through another creature's eyes.

Each transformation is considered a gift rather than a conquest. Druids do not steal the form of an animal—they earn its trust by understanding its place within the balance of the world. For this reason, many circles forbid careless or disrespectful use of Wild Shape, believing every transformation should honour the creature being emulated.

The oldest Archdruids teach that every new form reveals another lesson. To run as a wolf is to understand the strength of the pack. To soar as a hawk is to appreciate freedom. To swim as an otter is to embrace the endless flow of life itself.

---

> *"Do not become the beast to escape yourself. Become the beast to better understand the world you protect."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, First Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 2
### Description

Your understanding of the natural world has deepened, allowing you to adopt more capable and specialised beast forms. Every transformation feels more natural, requiring less concentration as your body and spirit learn to move as one.

With experience comes appreciation for the unique strengths of each creature. A wolf's endurance, a mountain goat's sure footing, or an otter's graceful swimming are no longer simply observed—they become your own. Every new form teaches another lesson about survival, adaptation, and the balance of nature.

The elders remind every Druid that Wild Shape is not measured by the number of forms they possess, but by how well they understand each one. A single mastered form is often more valuable than a dozen poorly understood transformations.

---

### Effects

- Spend **30 MP** to transform into a learned Beast Form.
- Wild Shape lasts for **15 minutes** or until dismissed.
- You may transform into **Small or Medium Beasts** that you have successfully learned.
- Learning a new Beast Form requires:
  - Observing the creature in its natural habitat.
  - Studying its behaviour and anatomy.
  - Succeeding on a **D20 Nature Check** with a DC determined by the Game Master.
- More elusive or dangerous beasts require higher DCs to learn.
- Once learned, a Beast Form is permanently added to your Wild Shape forms.
- While transformed:
  - You gain the beast's movement types, including climbing, swimming, burrowing, or limited gliding where appropriate.
  - You gain the beast's natural senses, such as enhanced smell, hearing, or low-light vision.
  - You retain your **Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma**.
  - You cannot cast spells.
  - You cannot speak languages unless the chosen form is capable of doing so.
  - Your equipment merges into your new form and provides no benefits unless specifically stated otherwise.
- If your Beast Form is reduced to **0 HP**, Wild Shape immediately ends and any remaining damage carries over to your normal Hit Points.
- You may voluntarily end Wild Shape at any time without using an action.

---

### Lore

As Druids continue along the Path of Wild Shape, they begin to realise that every creature has evolved to overcome different challenges. Strength alone is rarely the answer. The swift survive where the strong cannot, while the patient endure where the swift would fail.

Many circles encourage their apprentices to spend weeks living alongside the creatures they wish to emulate. They observe hunting patterns, migration routes, nesting habits, and social behaviour until the transformation becomes more than imitation—it becomes genuine understanding.

Among experienced Druids, each new Beast Form is viewed as another chapter in an endless story written by nature itself. Every transformation is both a privilege and a lesson, revealing another way life has adapted to thrive within the world of Asteria.

---

> *"To wear a beast's form without understanding its life is to wear only its skin. Learn its heart, and the transformation becomes complete."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, First Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 3
### Description

Your bond with the beasts of Asteria has matured into genuine kinship. Transformation no longer feels like assuming another shape—it feels as though you are remembering a part of yourself that has always existed within the natural world. Every heartbeat, instinct, and movement comes effortlessly, allowing you to adapt to the wilderness with remarkable confidence.

As your understanding grows, you may begin to study larger and more formidable creatures. These beasts demand greater patience and respect, for their instincts are stronger and their place within nature is more complex. Only Druids who truly understand a creature's purpose can successfully adopt its form.

Within many Druidic Circles, this stage marks the transition from student to guardian. You no longer transform simply to survive—you transform to fulfil the role each creature was born to perform, whether that is scouting, protecting, climbing, swimming, or enduring the harshest environments.

---

### Effects

- Spend **35 MP** to transform into a learned Beast Form.
- Wild Shape lasts for **20 minutes** or until dismissed.
- You may transform into **Small, Medium, or Large Beasts** that you have successfully learned.
- Learning a new Beast Form requires:
  - Observing the creature in its natural habitat.
  - Studying its behaviour, instincts, and anatomy.
  - Succeeding on a **D20 Nature Check** with a DC determined by the Game Master.
- Large or particularly elusive beasts require higher DCs and may require multiple successful observations before their form can be learned.
- Once learned, a Beast Form is permanently added to your Wild Shape forms.
- While transformed:
  - You gain the beast's movement types, natural senses, and non-magical physical abilities.
  - You retain your **Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma**.
  - You cannot cast spells.
  - You cannot speak languages unless the chosen form is physically capable of doing so.
  - Your equipment merges into your new form and provides no benefits unless specifically stated otherwise.
- If your Beast Form is reduced to **0 HP**, Wild Shape immediately ends and any remaining damage carries over to your normal Hit Points.
- You may voluntarily end Wild Shape at any time without using an action.

---

### Lore

Experienced Druids teach that every creature carries a lesson that cannot be learned through observation alone. To understand the endurance of a bear, one must feel the weight of its stride. To understand the patience of a hunting cat, one must wait without movement until the perfect moment arrives.

By this stage, Wild Shape has become more than a magical talent—it has become a spiritual discipline. Every new transformation broadens the Druid's understanding of life, revealing how countless species survive together while maintaining the balance of the natural world.

Among the oldest circles, it is believed that a Druid who truly honours every form they learn slowly becomes recognised by nature itself. Animals no longer see them as an outsider, but as another creature sharing the same ancient cycle of life.

---

> *"Every form you master teaches you how another soul survives. Respect each lesson, for nature wastes none."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, First Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 4
### Description

Your mastery of Wild Shape has reached a level few Druids ever achieve. Transformation is no longer a technique requiring deliberate thought; it has become second nature. Your body, mind, and spirit move as one, allowing you to fully embrace the instincts and capabilities of the creatures whose forms you have earned.

At this stage, even the most formidable beasts begin to reveal their secrets. Apex predators, mighty herbivores, and elusive creatures that have survived for decades within the wild may now become subjects of your study. Each new form demands unwavering patience, respect, and understanding, for powerful beasts rarely tolerate careless observation.

The elders teach that a Druid who reaches this stage no longer borrows the strength of nature—they become one of its trusted guardians, able to walk among its greatest creatures as an equal rather than an outsider.

---

### Effects

- Spend **40 MP** to transform into a learned Beast Form.
- Wild Shape lasts for **25 minutes** or until dismissed.
- You may transform into **Small, Medium, or Large Beasts**, including powerful apex predators, that you have successfully learned.
- Learning a new Beast Form requires:
  - Observing the creature within its natural habitat.
  - Understanding its behaviour, instincts, and role within the ecosystem.
  - Succeeding on one or more **D20 Nature Checks** with DCs determined by the Game Master.
- Rare, dangerous, or legendary beasts may require multiple successful observations across different encounters before their form can be learned.
- Once learned, a Beast Form is permanently added to your Wild Shape collection.
- While transformed:
  - You gain the beast's movement types, natural senses, and non-magical physical abilities.
  - You retain your **Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma**.
  - You cannot cast spells.
  - You cannot speak languages unless the chosen form is physically capable of doing so.
  - Your equipment merges into your new form and provides no benefits unless specifically stated otherwise.
- If your Beast Form is reduced to **0 HP**, Wild Shape immediately ends and any remaining damage carries over to your normal Hit Points.
- You may voluntarily end Wild Shape at any time without using an action.
- You gain **Advantage on D20 Nature Checks** made to study and learn new Beast Forms.

---

### Lore

Within the oldest Druidic Circles, this stage is known as **The Mantle of the Wild**. Those who achieve it are recognised not for the number of forms they possess, but for the depth of understanding they have cultivated with every creature they have become.

Many Grand Druids spend months observing a single beast before attempting to learn its form. They witness its hunts, its struggles, its role within the food chain, and the respect it commands from other creatures. Only then do they attempt the sacred transformation.

It is said that nature willingly shares its greatest guardians only with those who have proven they will never abuse their gift. Every transformation is a reminder that strength exists to preserve balance, never to dominate it.

---

> *"The greatest beasts are not feared because they are strong. They are respected because they know precisely when strength should be used."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, First Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 5
### Description

You have become one of the greatest shapeshifters of the Druidic Orders. Wild Shape is no longer simply a magical transformation—it is a perfect harmony between your spirit and the countless lives that inhabit the natural world. Every creature you have studied leaves a permanent imprint upon your soul, allowing you to call upon its form with absolute confidence.

The greatest beasts of Asteria are no longer beyond your understanding. Through years of observation, respect, and spiritual discipline, you have learned that every predator, every guardian, and every gentle giant exists to preserve the balance of nature. Their strength is not yours to command—it is yours to borrow with humility.

Those who reach this pinnacle are known throughout the ancient circles as **True Wildshapers**. Legends tell of Druids who crossed entire continents as migrating birds, defended villages as colossal bears, or vanished into the wilderness as wolves without ever revealing their true identities. To the beasts of the world, they are no longer strangers, but kindred spirits walking the same eternal cycle.

---

### Effects

- Spend **50 MP** to transform into a learned Beast Form.
- Wild Shape lasts for **30 minutes** or until dismissed.
- You may transform into **any Beast** that you have successfully learned, regardless of its size.
- Learning a new Beast Form requires:
  - Observing the creature in its natural habitat.
  - Understanding its behaviour, instincts, anatomy, and ecological role.
  - Completing one or more **D20 Nature Checks** with DCs determined by the Game Master.
- Exceptionally rare, ancient, or legendary beasts may require extended study over multiple encounters before their form can be learned.
- Once learned, a Beast Form is permanently added to your Wild Shape collection.
- While transformed:
  - You gain the beast's movement types, natural senses, and non-magical physical abilities.
  - You retain your **Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma**.
  - You cannot cast spells.
  - You cannot speak languages unless the chosen form is physically capable of doing so.
  - Your equipment merges into your new form and provides no benefits unless specifically stated otherwise.
- If your Beast Form is reduced to **0 HP**, Wild Shape immediately ends and any remaining damage carries over to your normal Hit Points.
- You may voluntarily end Wild Shape at any time without using an action.
- You have **Advantage on all D20 Nature Checks** made to study and learn new Beast Forms.
- Once per Long Rest, you may immediately transform into any previously learned Beast Form **without spending Mana**.

---

### Lore

The oldest Druidic texts describe this achievement as **The Soul of the Wild**. Few individuals in recorded history have reached this level of mastery, for it demands a lifetime of patience, compassion, and unwavering respect for every living creature. It is said that the forests themselves remember the footsteps of those who attain it.

Among the ancient circles, True Wildshapers are often entrusted with the protection of sacred groves, Worldroots, and places where the veil between the spirit world and nature grows thin. Their wisdom is sought not because they possess great power, but because they have lived countless lives through the forms they have mastered.

To witness a True Wildshaper transform is to watch nature itself flow effortlessly from one form to another. There is no flash of magic or violent surge of energy—only the quiet certainty that all living things are connected, and that the Druid has become part of that endless cycle.

---

> *"When you no longer ask how to become the beast, but instead remember that you have always been part of the wild, your journey is complete."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, First Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

# Living Forest

## Overview
Your connection to the natural world has grown so strong that the forest itself begins to answer your call.

Whenever you weave powerful plant-based Earth magic into the world, you leave behind traces of primal life. On rare occasions, that lingering energy gathers into a small guardian spirit known as an **Entling**. Though young and inexperienced, these spirits are fiercely loyal to those who protect the balance of nature.

Unlike summoned creatures created through spellcraft, an Entling is born naturally from the life energy awakened by your magic. It is not forced into service, but willingly answers the call of a Druid whose actions nurture the living world.

No two Entlings are exactly alike. Some resemble tiny saplings with glowing eyes, while others appear as moss-covered roots or walking shrubs. Their personalities are as varied as the forests from which they emerge.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

Your connection to the natural world has grown so strong that the forest itself begins to answer your call.

Whenever you weave powerful plant-based Earth magic into the world, you leave behind traces of primal life. On rare occasions, that lingering energy gathers into a small guardian spirit known as an **Entling**. Though young and inexperienced, these spirits are fiercely loyal to those who protect the balance of nature.

Unlike summoned creatures created through spellcraft, an Entling is born naturally from the life energy awakened by your magic. It is not forced into service, but willingly answers the call of a Druid whose actions nurture the living world.

No two Entlings are exactly alike. Some resemble tiny saplings with glowing eyes, while others appear as moss-covered roots or walking shrubs. Their personalities are as varied as the forests from which they emerge.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- Whenever you cast a **plant-based Earth spell** that alters or affects the environment, you may make a **Luck Check (DC 16)**.
- **Talent-based cantrips do not trigger this effect.**
- On a successful check, an **Entling** is summoned in an unoccupied space within the spell's affected area.
- The Entling is treated as a **Summon** and acts immediately after your turn.
- The Entling follows your verbal or telepathic commands where possible.
- Only **one Entling** may be summoned through this talent at a time.
- If an Entling is already active, additional successful Luck Checks have no effect until it is dismissed or defeated.

---

### Lore

The oldest Druidic Circles tell stories of forests so ancient that they developed spirits of their own. These spirits watched over the woodland for centuries, protecting every seedling, beast, and stream within their domain.

Most Druids never witness such beings, but those whose bond with nature is exceptionally strong occasionally attract younger forest spirits seeking purpose.

Known as Entlings, these tiny guardians are believed to be the first heartbeat of a future forest guardian. They are curious, protective, and deeply connected to the life that surrounds them.

Many Druids consider the arrival of their first Entling to be a sacred milestone, for it is said that the forest has chosen to walk beside them.

---

> *"You cannot command a forest to trust you. When an Entling chooses to stand at your side, know that the forest already has."*  
> — **Archdruid Elarion Wildroot, Guardian of the First Grove**

## Rank 2
### Description

Your bond with the forest deepens, attracting stronger guardian spirits to your side.

The young Entling that once answered your magic has matured into a **Sapling Ent**. While still considered a juvenile among its ancient kin, it possesses greater strength, resilience, and intelligence than its smaller predecessor.

The forest continues to decide when one of its guardians should answer your call. Every spell that nourishes or reshapes the natural world carries the possibility of awakening another dormant spirit.

Many Druids believe this transformation is not simply the growth of a summoned creature, but evidence that the same forest spirit continues to mature alongside its chosen guardian.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- Whenever you cast a **plant-based Earth spell** that alters or affects the environment, you may make a **Luck Check (DC 15)**.
- **Talent-based cantrips do not trigger this effect.**
- On a successful check, a **Sapling Ent** is summoned in an unoccupied space within the spell's affected area.
- The Sapling Ent replaces the Entling gained from Rank 1.
- The Sapling Ent is treated as a **Summon** and acts immediately after your turn.
- The Sapling Ent follows your verbal or telepathic commands.
- Only **one Living Forest summon** may exist at a time.
- The Sapling Ent is larger, tougher, and more capable than an Entling, making it a more reliable forest guardian.

---

### Lore

Druidic texts describe Sapling Ents as the first true guardians of the woodland.

Unlike Entlings, which are curious and playful spirits, Sapling Ents begin to understand their purpose. They instinctively defend healthy forests, protect wildlife, and stand against those who seek to destroy the balance of nature.

Some ancient groves are said to contain Sapling Ents that have remained in the same clearing for centuries, patiently waiting until a worthy Druid awakens their dormant spirit.

Among the Verdant Circles, it is believed that a Sapling Ent chooses its Druid just as much as the Druid earns the trust of the forest.

---

> *"The first spirit follows because it is curious. The second remains because it believes in you."*  
> — **Elder Rowan Ashgrove, Keeper of the Emerald Path**

## Rank 3
### Description

Your connection to the Living Forest continues to flourish, allowing ancient woodland spirits to place greater trust in your magic.

When the forest answers your call, it now manifests as a **Young Ent**—a powerful guardian that has matured beyond its sapling years. Stronger, wiser, and deeply connected to the natural world, a Young Ent acts as both protector and caretaker of the land.

Unlike its smaller predecessors, a Young Ent possesses a keen understanding of its surroundings. It instinctively shields allies, disrupts those who threaten nature, and helps preserve the balance wherever it walks.

Many Druids believe that each time a Young Ent answers their call, it is the same spirit continuing its journey alongside them. As the Druid grows in wisdom, so too does the guardian that walks beside them.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- Whenever you cast a **plant-based Earth spell** that alters or affects the environment, you may make a **Luck Check (DC 14)**.
- **Talent-based cantrips do not trigger this effect.**
- On a successful check, a **Young Ent** is summoned in an unoccupied space within the spell's affected area.
- The Young Ent replaces the Sapling Ent gained from Rank 2.
- The Young Ent is treated as a **Summon** and acts immediately after your turn.
- The Young Ent follows your verbal or telepathic commands.
- Only **one Living Forest summon** may exist at a time.
- The Young Ent gains improved Health, Defence, and Damage compared to the Sapling Ent.
- While the Young Ent is active, allied creatures within **5 metres** of it gain **+2 to saving throws against forced movement and knockback effects**, as the guardian steadies the ground with its living roots.

---

### Lore

Young Ents are regarded by many Druidic Circles as the first true wardens of the forest.

They patrol ancient woodlands, guide lost creatures back to safety, and silently watch over sacred groves that have stood for generations. Although peaceful by nature, they become relentless defenders whenever the balance of nature is threatened.

Old tales claim that Young Ents can recognise the footsteps of those who respect the wild, allowing them to pass unhindered, while those who seek to burn, poison, or corrupt the forest quickly earn their attention.

To stand beside a Young Ent is considered an honour, for few woodland spirits choose to accompany a mortal for long.

---

> *"A sapling grows because the forest wills it. An Ent grows because the forest trusts it."*  
> — **Archdruid Thalen Mossroot, Warden of the Elder Groves**

## Rank 4
### Description

Your bond with the Living Forest has become so profound that ancient guardian spirits willingly answer your call.

The forest now sends forth an **Ancient Ent**, a venerable protector whose presence alone commands respect from the creatures of the wild. Towering over the battlefield, it embodies centuries of growth, resilience, and unwavering devotion to the balance of nature.

An Ancient Ent is more than a guardian—it is a steward of the forest. Wherever it walks, plant life flourishes, roots awaken beneath the soil, and the surrounding woodland responds to its presence. Many Druids believe these guardians carry the memories of forgotten forests and the wisdom of countless seasons.

To summon such a being is considered one of the greatest honours a Druid can receive before earning the trust of the legendary Elder Ents.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- Whenever you cast a **plant-based Earth spell** that alters or affects the environment, you may make a **Luck Check (DC 13)**.
- **Talent-based cantrips do not trigger this effect.**
- On a successful check, an **Ancient Ent** is summoned in an unoccupied space within the spell's affected area.
- The Ancient Ent replaces the Young Ent gained from Rank 3.
- The Ancient Ent is treated as a **Summon** and acts immediately after your turn.
- The Ancient Ent follows your verbal or telepathic commands.
- Only **one Living Forest summon** may exist at a time.
- The Ancient Ent possesses significantly greater Health, Defence, and Strength than previous forms.
- While the Ancient Ent is active, allied creatures within **10 metres** gain **+2 to Nature-based D20 Checks** and have **advantage on checks made to resist forced movement caused by natural terrain or plant-based effects.**
- Plant-based Earth spells cast within **10 metres** of the Ancient Ent have their **range increased by 5 metres**, as the guardian channels the surrounding forest to aid your magic.

---

### Lore

Ancient Ents are among the oldest living guardians of Asteria's forests. Some are believed to have stood watch since before the first kingdoms were founded, silently protecting sacred groves from war, corruption, and time itself.

Unlike younger forest spirits, Ancient Ents possess remarkable patience. They do not judge mortals by words alone but by years of action. Only Druids who have consistently shown respect for the natural world are ever deemed worthy of their companionship.

Within Druidic Circles, the appearance of an Ancient Ent is celebrated as proof that the forest no longer sees the Druid as a visitor, but as one of its own protectors.

---

> *"When an Ancient Ent answers your call, remember this—it is not obeying you. It has simply decided that your purpose is worthy of its strength."*  
> — **High Grovekeeper Sylvara Rootheart, Circle of the Living Canopy**

## Rank 5
### Description

Your bond with the Living Forest has reached its pinnacle, earning the trust of one of nature's greatest guardians—the **Elder Ent**.

These colossal beings are spoken of only in ancient Druidic legends. They are the oldest protectors of the wild, having watched forests grow, kingdoms rise, and civilizations fade beneath their branches. An Elder Ent does not answer the call of power alone. It answers only those who have proven themselves faithful stewards of the natural world.

Whenever the forest chooses to awaken, an Elder Ent emerges as a living embodiment of nature's will. Its presence inspires nearby wildlife, strengthens the land itself, and reminds all who stand before it that the forest has never truly been defenceless.

Many Druids spend their entire lives hoping to witness an Elder Ent. Those fortunate enough to fight beside one are remembered throughout history as Wardens of the Living Forest.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- Whenever you cast a **plant-based Earth spell** that alters or affects the environment, you may make a **Luck Check (DC 12)**.
- **Talent-based cantrips do not trigger this effect.**
- On a successful check, an **Elder Ent** is summoned in an unoccupied space within the spell's affected area.
- The Elder Ent replaces the Ancient Ent gained from Rank 4.
- The Elder Ent is treated as a **Summon** and acts immediately after your turn.
- The Elder Ent follows your verbal or telepathic commands.
- Only **one Living Forest summon** may exist at a time.
- The Elder Ent possesses exceptional Health, Defence, and Strength, making it one of the most resilient natural guardians a Druid can summon.

While the Elder Ent is active:

- Allied creatures within **15 metres** gain **+3 to Nature-related D20 Checks**.
- Plant-based Earth spells cast within **15 metres** of the Elder Ent have their range increased by **10 metres**.
- Difficult Terrain created by your Earth or Plant spells does not affect you or your allies.
- Once per turn, when you cast a **Life** or **Earth** spell within the Elder Ent's aura, you may reduce its Mana Cost by **2 MP** as the Elder Ent channels the surrounding natural energy into your magic.

---

### Lore

Elder Ents are believed to be among the oldest living beings in Asteria. Some legends claim they were already ancient when the first Druids learned to speak with the forest.

Unlike younger Ents, they rarely leave the sacred groves they protect. Their appearance is considered an omen that the natural world has recognised a worthy guardian and chosen to lend its strength.

Every scar carved into an Elder Ent's bark tells the story of a forest defended, a wildfire endured, or a kingdom reclaimed by nature. They are living monuments to the resilience of the wild.

Among the oldest Druidic Circles, becoming a companion to an Elder Ent is regarded as one of the greatest honours a protector of nature can receive.

---

> *"An Elder Ent does not answer because you called. It answers because the forest believes you are worth protecting."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Elarion Wildroot, Guardian of the First Grove**

# Nature's Wrath

## Overview
The natural world rewards those who fight in harmony with it. Every spell you weave through the earth, every vine you command, and every blossom you nurture awakens a fragment of the forest's primal power.

This energy manifests as **Wrath Points**, representing the growing determination of the wild to preserve its balance. Rather than exploding uncontrollably, you may channel this energy to strengthen your spells at the moment they are cast.

Experienced Druids know that true strength lies not in overwhelming force, but in knowing when to release the power nature has entrusted to them.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

The natural world rewards those who fight in harmony with it. Every spell you weave through the earth, every vine you command, and every blossom you nurture awakens a fragment of the forest's primal power.

This energy manifests as **Wrath Points**, representing the growing determination of the wild to preserve its balance. Rather than exploding uncontrollably, you may channel this energy to strengthen your spells at the moment they are cast.

Experienced Druids know that true strength lies not in overwhelming force, but in knowing when to release the power nature has entrusted to them.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- Whenever you successfully cast a **Life** or **Earth** spell, gain **1 Wrath Point**.
- You may have a maximum of **10 Wrath Points**.
- Wrath Points **resets every short rest**.
- You may only spend Wrath Points while casting a **Life** or **Earth** spell.
- Only **one Wrath Technique** may be applied to a spell.

#### Wrath Techniques

When casting a qualifying spell, you may choose **one** of the following:

**Deep Roots** *(2 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's range by **5 metres**.

**Primal Focus** *(3 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's **Spell Save DC by +1**.

**Verdant Surge** *(4 Wrath Points)*
- Add an additional **+1D4** damage or healing spells.

---

### Lore

The oldest Druids teach that nature is neither cruel nor kind—it simply seeks balance. Every spell cast in defence of that balance leaves behind a trace of primal energy, gathering quietly within those who respect the wild.

Unlike raw mana, this energy cannot be forced into existence. It must be earned through action, patience, and harmony with the natural world. Those who rush to spend it too quickly find only fleeting strength, while those who learn restraint discover that even the smallest seed can one day become an ancient forest.

To master Nature's Wrath is not to command the anger of the wild, but to become its trusted steward.

---

> *"The forest gives you its strength one leaf at a time. Wisdom is knowing which leaf to spend."*  
> — **Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 2
### Description

Your understanding of Nature's Wrath deepens, allowing you to shape the wild's energy with greater precision. The primal essence gathered through your spells no longer seeks only to empower your magic—it begins to respond to your intentions.

As your bond with the natural world strengthens, you learn to conserve the forest's fury until the perfect moment. Every Wrath Point becomes another root in the growing strength of your magic, ready to be woven into your next spell.

Experienced Druids rarely spend their Wrath carelessly. Instead, they allow it to build naturally, choosing the enhancement that best suits the situation before them.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- Whenever you successfully cast a **Life** or **Earth** spell, gain **1 Wrath Point**.
- You may have a maximum of **10 Wrath Points**.
- Wrath Points are removed at the end of combat.
- You may only spend Wrath Points while casting a **Life** or **Earth** spell.
- Only **one Wrath Technique** may be applied to a spell.

#### Wrath Techniques

**Deep Roots** *(2 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's range by **5 metres**.

**Primal Focus** *(3 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's **Spell Save DC by +1**.

**Verdant Surge** *(4 Wrath Points)*
- Add an additional **+1D4** damage or healing spells.

**Enduring Growth** *(5 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's duration by **1 Round**.

---

### Lore

As Druids mature, they come to realise that the forest's power is not measured by how quickly it grows, but by how wisely it is used.

The oldest wardens compare Wrath to the changing seasons. It gathers slowly, almost unnoticed, before revealing its full strength when the moment is right. Those who master this balance learn to shape the battlefield without wasting the gifts the natural world has entrusted to them.

Within the Circle of the Emerald Wilds, young Druids are taught that every Wrath Point represents the trust of the forest. Spending it recklessly is seen as no different than cutting down an ancient tree for firewood.

---

> *"Power borrowed from the wild should never be wasted. The forest remembers every gift it gives."*  
> — **Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 3
### Description

The bond between you and the natural world has grown beyond simple harmony. The Wrath you gather is no longer merely energy waiting to be spent—it has become an extension of your will, flowing through your magic with remarkable control.

Experienced Druids learn that nature is at its strongest when it can endure. Rather than always seeking to strike harder, they learn to preserve life, strengthen their allies, and ensure that every spell leaves a lasting impact upon the battlefield.

Every Wrath Point spent is another expression of the forest's trust, allowing your magic to flourish in exactly the way the moment demands.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- Whenever you successfully cast a **Life** or **Earth** spell, gain **1 Wrath Point**.
- You may have a maximum of **10 Wrath Points**.
- Wrath Points are removed at the end of combat.
- You may only spend Wrath Points while casting a **Life** or **Earth** spell.
- Only **one Wrath Technique** may be applied to a spell.

#### Wrath Techniques

- Increase the spell's range by **10 metres**.

**Primal Focus** *(3 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's **Spell Save DC by +1**.

**Verdant Surge** *(4 Wrath Points)*
- Add an additional **+1D4** damage or healing spells.

**Enduring Growth** *(5 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's duration by **1 Rounds**.

**Nature's Resilience** *(6 Wrath Points)*
- When casting a **Life** or **Earth** spell on yourself or an ally, grant **Temporary 5 Hit points** to target.
- Temporary HP gained this way lasts until the end of combat or until depleted.

---

### Lore

The oldest wardens believed that true mastery over Nature's Wrath was not measured by how much destruction a Druid could unleash, but by how wisely they chose to wield the gifts of the wild.

Every root that breaks stone also supports the forest above it. Every towering tree survives because its roots protect it long before danger arrives. Druids who reach this level of mastery begin to understand that nature's greatest strength has always been its resilience.

Among the Emerald Circles, this lesson marks the transition from apprentice to guardian. From this point onward, a Druid no longer fights for the forest alone—they fight as one of its protectors.

---

> *"The strongest roots are never seen. Yet without them, no forest could ever stand."*  
> — **High Warden Elowen Briarroot, Circle of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 4
### Description

Your mastery over Nature's Wrath has become instinctive. The primal energy gathered through your magic flows effortlessly, allowing you to weave the forest's power into every spell with remarkable precision.

The natural world no longer simply lends you its strength—it trusts your judgement. Every Wrath Point represents the growing will of the wild, waiting to be shaped into exactly the form the moment demands.

Veteran Druids rarely exhaust their Wrath through reckless displays of power. Instead, they reserve it for the decisive moment, empowering the spell that will protect their allies, reshape the battlefield, or bring an end to the conflict.

To the oldest Druidic Circles, this level of mastery marks the beginning of becoming a true Warden of Nature.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- Whenever you successfully cast a **Life** or **Earth** spell, gain **1 Wrath Point**.
- You may have a maximum of **15 Wrath Points**.
- Wrath Points are removed at the end of combat.
- You may only spend Wrath Points while casting a **Life** or **Earth** spell.

- Increase the spell's **Spell Save DC by +2**.

**Verdant Surge** *(4 Wrath Points)*
- Add an additional **+1D6** damage or healing spells.

**Enduring Growth** *(5 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's duration by **2 Rounds**.

**Nature's Resilience** *(6 Wrath Points)*
- When casting a **Life** or **Earth** spell on yourself or an ally, grant **Temporary 5 Hit points** to target.
- Temporary HP gained this way lasts until the end of combat or until depleted.

**Primal Awakening** *(8 Wrath Points)*
Choose one when casting a qualifying spell:
- The spell **ignores Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover**.
- One **Plant-based Summon** you control may immediately move up to its Speed and make **one Basic Attack** as a free action.

---

### Lore

The oldest guardians believed the forest rewards wisdom above all else. It does not ask its protectors to unleash power at every opportunity, but to recognise the single moment when that power will matter most.

Druids who reach this stage are often entrusted with defending sacred groves, ancient Worldroots, and places where the balance of nature is most fragile. Their command of Nature's Wrath is no longer driven by instinct alone, but by centuries of teachings passed from one generation of wardens to the next.

To witness such a Druid in battle is to watch the wild itself respond with perfect timing. Every spell, every vine, and every bloom seems to arrive exactly when it is needed.

---

> *"The forest does not waste a single leaf. Neither should a Druid waste a single fragment of its strength."*  
> — **Grand Warden Sylvara Thornheart, Keeper of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 5
### Description

You have mastered the primal energies of the natural world, becoming a true Warden of the Wild. Every spell you cast leaves an imprint upon the land, and every Wrath Point you gather represents the trust the forest has placed in you.

No longer content with minor blessings, the natural world now allows you to channel its full might through a single spell. This ultimate technique, known simply as **Nature's Wrath**, is not an attack of rage but a perfect expression of harmony between Druid and nature.

The oldest Archdruids teach that Nature's Wrath should never be used lightly. It is a gift earned through patience, wisdom, and respect for the balance of life. When unleashed, the battlefield itself seems to answer your call, amplifying your magic beyond its normal limits.

Few Druids ever reach this level of mastery, and those who do are remembered as legends among the circles of Asteria.

---

- Increase the spell's duration by **3 Rounds**.

- When casting a **Life** or **Earth** spell on yourself or an ally, grant **Temporary 10 Hit points** to target.

**Nature's Precision** (10 Wrath Points)

---

The oldest Druidic Circles believe that Nature's Wrath is not born from anger, but from perfect balance. It is the moment when every root, stone, flower, and tree willingly lends its strength to a single purpose.

Legends tell of Archdruids who ended battles without drawing blood, simply by commanding the forest to reclaim the land beneath invading armies. Others speak of healers whose Life magic became so overwhelming that entire companies rose to their feet beneath a single blossom.

To wield Nature's Wrath is to carry the trust of the wild itself. Such power is never demanded—it is given only to those who have spent a lifetime protecting the balance they now command.

# Rooted Power

## Overview
You learn to draw strength directly from the earth beneath your feet. By remaining perfectly still, your roots of mana extend into the land, allowing you to channel greater power through your Earth magic.

Although remaining stationary leaves you vulnerable, the reward is greater control and destructive potential. Experienced Druids often prepare themselves before unleashing powerful spells, allowing the land itself to amplify their magic.

Rooted Power reflects one of the oldest teachings of the Druidic Circles: the strongest tree is not the one that moves with every wind, but the one whose roots run deepest.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

You learn to draw strength directly from the earth beneath your feet. By remaining perfectly still, your roots of mana extend into the land, allowing you to channel greater power through your Earth magic.

Although remaining stationary leaves you vulnerable, the reward is greater control and destructive potential. Experienced Druids often prepare themselves before unleashing powerful spells, allowing the land itself to amplify their magic.

Rooted Power reflects one of the oldest teachings of the Druidic Circles: the strongest tree is not the one that moves with every wind, but the one whose roots run deepest.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- If you **do not move during your turn**, you become **Rooted** until the start of your next turn.
- While Rooted:
  - Your **Earth spells** gain **+2 Damage**.
  - Any **Earth spell** that requires a **D20 Saving Throw** increases its **Save DC by +2**.
  - Earth spells that create **Difficult Terrain** or alter the battlefield have their duration increased by **1 Round**.
- Moving before casting immediately removes the Rooted bonus.
- This talent affects **Earth spells only**.

---

### Lore

Among the oldest Druids, standing motionless before casting is not seen as hesitation—it is seen as respect. They believe the earth willingly shares its strength only with those patient enough to listen.

Many ancient stone circles were built as places where Druids could root themselves to the land before performing powerful rituals. Even today, experienced practitioners pause for a brief moment before calling upon the deepest powers of the earth.

To outsiders, the Druid appears perfectly still. Beneath the surface, however, invisible currents of natural magic flow through the ground, gathering around them until released in a single overwhelming spell.

---

> *"The mountain does not seek power. It simply stands, and power gathers around it."*  
> — **Archdruid Thalen Stoneroot, Warden of the Emerald Peaks**

## Rank 2
### Description

Your roots reach deeper into the earth, allowing greater amounts of natural energy to flow through your body before being released as powerful Earth magic.

The longer you remain still, the more stable your connection becomes. Rather than forcing mana into your spells, you allow the land itself to strengthen them. Every stone, root, and grain of soil beneath your feet becomes part of your magic.

Veteran Druids often choose their ground carefully before combat begins. Once rooted, they become living conduits of the earth, capable of shaping the battlefield with remarkable precision.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- If you **do not move during your turn**, you become **Rooted** until the start of your next turn.
- While Rooted:
  - Your **Earth spells** gain **+4 Damage**.
  - Any **Earth spell** that requires a **D20 Saving Throw** increases its **Save DC by +3**.
  - Earth spells that create **Difficult Terrain** or alter the battlefield have their duration increased by **2 Rounds**.
  - The range of your Earth spells increases by **5 metres**.
- Moving before casting immediately removes the Rooted bonuses.
- This talent affects **Earth spells only**.

---

### Lore

As Druids continue their training, they discover that true strength does not come from standing firm—it comes from becoming part of the land itself.

Every heartbeat, every breath, and every pulse of mana sinks into the earth before returning many times stronger. Ancient Druids believed that the land remembers those who stand with patience, rewarding them with power that cannot be gained through haste alone.

Many sacred stone circles throughout Asteria were built for this very purpose, allowing Druids to root themselves in places where the world's natural energies are strongest.

---

> *"The earth gives freely to those willing to stand and listen. Those who rush hear only silence."*  
> — **Stonewarden Brynn Earthsong, Circle of the Ancient Stones**

## Rank 3
### Description

Your bond with the earth has become second nature. The moment you plant your feet, invisible roots of mana spread deep beneath the ground, drawing strength from the land and feeding it into your spells.

The earth no longer simply empowers your magic—it stabilises it. Every spell is cast with greater force and precision, while the ground itself resists any attempt to move you from your chosen position.

Experienced Druids know that sacrificing mobility is a small price to pay for commanding the overwhelming power of the earth. Once rooted, they become as steadfast as the mountains they call upon.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- If you **do not move during your turn**, you become **Rooted** until the start of your next turn.
- While Rooted:
  - Your **Earth spells** gain **+6 Damage**.
  - Any **Earth spell** that requires a **D20 Saving Throw** increases its **Save DC by +4**.
  - The range of your Earth spells increases by **10 metres**.
  - Earth spells that create **Difficult Terrain** or alter the battlefield have their duration increased by **3 Rounds**.
  - You gain **Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws** made to resist being **pushed, pulled, knocked prone, or forcibly moved**.
- Moving before casting immediately removes all Rooted bonuses.
- This talent affects **Earth spells only**.

---

### Lore

The oldest Druids speak of becoming one with the mountains—not in body, but in spirit. Through years of practice, they learn to anchor themselves so completely that even powerful magic struggles to break their connection with the earth.

Many legendary battles tell of Druids standing unmoved while the world around them crumbled. Storms raged, armies charged, and the ground split beneath their feet, yet they remained steadfast, drawing endless strength from the land below.

Among the Circle of Stone, reaching this level of Rooted Power marks the beginning of true Earth mastery, where patience becomes strength and stillness becomes power.

---

> *"A mountain does not resist the storm because it is stronger. It endures because it refuses to move."*  
> — **Stonewarden Brynn Earthsong, Circle of the Ancient Stones**

## Rank 4
### Description

Your connection to the earth has become unwavering. The moment you root yourself, the land embraces you as one of its own, anchoring your body and amplifying every Earth spell you cast.

The natural mana flowing beneath the surface surges through you with incredible force, allowing your spells to reshape the battlefield with unmatched precision. Stone walls rise taller, fissures spread farther, and every tremor carries greater destructive force.

Few enemies can move a Druid who has mastered this level of Rooted Power. They stand as immovable pillars amidst chaos, drawing strength from the world itself while unleashing the fury of the earth.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- If you **do not move during your turn**, you become **Rooted** until the start of your next turn.
- While Rooted:
  - Your **Earth spells** gain **+8 Damage**.
  - Any **Earth spell** that requires a **D20 Saving Throw** increases its **Save DC by +5**.
  - The range of your Earth spells increases by **15 metres**.
  - Earth spells that create **Difficult Terrain** or alter the battlefield have their duration increased by **4 Rounds**.
  - You gain **Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws** made to resist being **pushed, pulled, knocked prone, or forcibly moved**.
  - You gain **Resistance to Forced Movement**. If an effect would move you, reduce the distance by **half** (rounded down).
- Moving before casting immediately removes all Rooted bonuses.
- This talent affects **Earth spells only**.

---

### Lore

The ancient Stone Circles teach that the earth is never truly still. Beneath every mountain and valley lies an endless current of natural power, waiting for those patient enough to become part of it.

Druids who master Rooted Power are no longer visitors upon the land—they are accepted by it. Their footsteps become lighter, yet their presence becomes impossible to ignore. Even the oldest mountains recognise them as guardians rather than wanderers.

Legends tell of Druids who stood alone against charging armies, refusing to yield a single step. Though battered by wind, steel, and magic, they remained rooted until the battle was won, their unwavering resolve becoming as legendary as the mountains themselves.

---

> *"A tree survives because of its roots. A mountain endures because it has nowhere else to be. Learn from both."*  
> — **High Stonewarden Kaelor Granitebloom, Circle of the Worldroot**

## Rank 5
### Description

Your mastery of Earth magic reaches its pinnacle. The moment you root yourself, your body becomes one with the land beneath you, drawing upon the endless strength of the world itself. The flow of natural mana is no longer merely borrowed—it is welcomed, amplified, and released through you with overwhelming force.

While rooted, every Earth spell is cast with exceptional precision and destructive power. The ground answers your call without hesitation, raising walls of stone, opening deep fissures, and reshaping the battlefield as though the land itself has become your ally.

The oldest Druids refer to this state as becoming **Worldrooted**. Few ever achieve it, for it requires complete trust in the natural world. Those who do are said to stand as living pillars between civilisation and the untamed wilds, immovable until they choose to walk once more.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- If you **do not move during your turn**, you become **Rooted** until the start of your next turn.
- While Rooted:
  - Your **Earth spells** gain **+10 Damage**.
  - Any **Earth spell** that requires a **D20 Saving Throw** increases its **Save DC by +6**.
  - The range of your Earth spells increases by **20 metres**.
  - Earth spells that create **Difficult Terrain** or alter the battlefield have their duration increased by **5 Rounds**.
  - You gain **Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws** made to resist being **pushed, pulled, knocked prone, or forcibly moved**.
  - You **cannot be forcibly moved** by non-legendary abilities or effects while Rooted.
  - Your Earth spells ignore **Half Cover** and **Three-Quarters Cover** created by natural terrain.
- Moving before casting immediately removes all Rooted bonuses.
- This talent affects **Earth spells only**.

---

### Lore

To become Worldrooted is to earn the complete trust of the earth itself. The oldest legends speak of Druids who stood unmoving for days upon sacred mountains, allowing their spirits to intertwine with the heartbeat of the world until they could no longer tell where they ended and the land began.

These Druids became living extensions of the earth. Wherever they stood, stone rose to defend them, cliffs answered their commands, and the ground itself refused to allow them to fall.

Modern Druids rarely witness such mastery, yet every Circle preserves the stories as a reminder that true power is not found in movement or speed, but in unwavering resolve. The earth has endured since the beginning of Asteria, and those who become one with it inherit a fraction of that timeless strength.

---

> *"Stand long enough for the world to know your name, and one day it will answer when you call."*  
> — **Grand Earthwarden Kaelor Granitebloom, Keeper of the Worldroot**

None
